allies.rationale_text: Schema-acquisition supports perceptual-learning by turning repeated cue exposure into stable patterns that can be retrieved and updated later.
allies.source_quote: Its core definition and purpose involve the development of mental models or schemas that represent external reality.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: PL is 'the engine that builds these models', converting observations into compressed, usable structure — essential mechanism.
allies.activation_condition: When building domain expertise through repeated observation and pattern recognition that solidifies into reusable schemas.

allies.rationale_text: Cognitive-load-theory supports perceptual-learning by freeing working memory so meaningful cues can consolidate into usable patterns.
allies.source_quote: PL reduces cognitive load. By developing stable patterns and chunks of information, the working memory is freed up.
allies.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'PL reduces cognitive load' by developing stable patterns and chunks, freeing working memory for new schema formation.
allies.activation_condition: When complex information needs to be chunked into manageable patterns to reduce working memory demand.

antagonists.rationale_text: Einstellung-effect undermines perceptual-learning by causing the brain to lock onto a previously learned pattern and torture new stimuli to fit it, blocking the updated discrimination that perceptual learning requires.
antagonists.source_quote: Over-reliance on existing, well-developed mental models leads one to torture reality so that it fits your models. Experts sometimes persist in using frames that are unhelpful or misleading when encountering genuinely novel problems.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Curated tension: prior pattern expectations suppress anomaly detection; established perceptual templates resist updating.
antagonists.activation_condition: When established perceptual patterns suppress detection of novel anomalies or contradicting evidence.

antagonists.rationale_text: Curse-of-knowledge undermines perceptual-learning by making refined perceptual schemas impossible to communicate to novices, blocking the transfer of expert pattern recognition that the model is built to enable.
antagonists.source_quote: Experts, having refined their models through PL, find it difficult to remember what it was like not to know something. This high-level, abstract thinking conflicts with the need to communicate clearly with novices.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Canonical: 'experts find it difficult to remember what it was like *not* to know something' — high-level abstraction hinders novice communication.
antagonists.activation_condition: When expert-level pattern recognition creates difficulty communicating insights to novice audiences.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Perceptual-learning conflicts with confirmation-bias when prior pattern expectations suppress anomaly detection.
structured_tensions.source_quote: perceptual-learning vs confirmation-bias: perceptual-learning conflicts with confirmation-bias (confirmation bias) when prior pattern expectations suppress anomaly detection.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Perceptual-learning conflicts with status-quo-bias when practitioners stop updating their pattern libraries after initial mastery.
structured_tensions.source_quote: perceptual-learning vs status-quo-bias: perceptual-learning conflicts with status-quo-bias (status quo bias) when practitioners stop updating pattern libraries after initial mastery.
